title: How a run names its body, its profile and its target window
description: Produced by SP-2 (a loop change), consumed by SP-4 and SP-5. Today these three cannot be combined: `window` is rejected unless device is the literal string 'windows' (agent/loop.py:164), a forced profile builds its body with no window (agent/loop.py:190), a Device instance means no profile loads at all (agent/loop.py:192), and the task API rejects `window` without an explicit device (api/server.py:61). After SP-2, a named window selects the host body, the catalog supplies the app profile, and a host run with no window is refused rather than run unguarded.

device.description: A body name: android, linux, windows. Omit to let the picker choose.

profile.description: A profile path, or several; each must resolve to profiles/<path>/profile.md. The top segment also names the body.

window.description: A window title substring or an hwnd selector. Naming it selects the host body, so a caller does not have to name the device, and it is what keeps a title match from landing on the wrong document. A host run without one is refused, because both host guards are no-ops when no target is named.

then.description: When a window is named, anything else named must agree that this is the host body; window alone is valid and selects it.

x-invariants: A run whose resolved body is windows MUST name a window; otherwise it is refused before the first action.
RESERVED: `unreal` calls go through the action contract, not this one.
